# holt — THE GUARD CORPUS.
#
# These are the test files that prove holt does not destroy work: the destructive-command
# classifier, the in-place-destruction guards (reset --hard, clean -fd, checkout -- ., restore),
# the read-only contract, the lock/unprotect path, the stash evidence trail, the verify
# interaction engine, the invariant fuzzer, and the adversarial corpus that puts the repository
# into states nobody designed for.
#
# WHY A FILE AND NOT A LIST INSIDE ci.yml. The list used to be hand-typed into one `node --test`
# line in one job. test/e2e/adversarial.test.mjs was not on it, so the single most
# platform-sensitive suite in the repository reached Windows and macOS only by being swept up in
# `npm test`'s `test/**/*.test.mjs` glob in a different job. That is coverage by accident, and it
# is the kind that disappears without a failing build:
#
#   $ node --test "test/nonexistent/**/*.test.mjs"; echo $?
#   ℹ pass 0
#   0
#
# A glob that matches nothing exits 0. A green `npm test` is therefore not evidence that any
# particular file ran. scripts/run-guard-corpus.mjs reads THIS file, refuses to start if any
# entry is missing, and runs the named files explicitly on every OS in the matrix.
# scripts/check-ci-hardening.mjs fails the build if that step is not wired into a job that runs on
# ubuntu-latest, macos-latest AND windows-latest.
#
# FOUR distinct Windows path bugs have been found in this project. This is where a fifth shows up.
#
# Every file below is proven to pass with NO optional backends installed (no ctags, no enry, no
# jscpd, no jj), because the job that runs this corpus is the degraded-core job. A file that needs
# a backend belongs in the full-suite job instead.

test/unit/safety.test.mjs
test/e2e/detection.test.mjs
test/e2e/cli.test.mjs
test/e2e/actions.test.mjs
test/e2e/fuzz-invariant.test.mjs
test/e2e/integration.test.mjs
test/e2e/adversarial.test.mjs
test/e2e/break-it.test.mjs
test/e2e/strict-read-only.test.mjs
test/e2e/unprotect-force.test.mjs
test/e2e/stash-evidence.test.mjs
test/e2e/verify.test.mjs
# BOTH HALVES OF THE BAR IN ONE FILE. It proves — by running the real programs — that a
# dry-run/usage invocation destroys nothing and is allowed, that the spellings which only LOOK
# like dry runs really do delete and are still refused, and that a 360-command corpus of ordinary
# developer work is allowed silently. A false positive is as serious as a missed destroyer, and
# this is where a regression in either direction shows up.
test/e2e/no-op-invocations.test.mjs
test/e2e/decision-integrity.test.mjs
test/e2e/guard-classes-repair.test.mjs
